name: Riders of Rohan
oracle_text:
When this creature enters, create two 2/2 red Human Knight creature tokens with trample and haste.
Dash {4}{R}{W} (You may cast this spell for its dash cost. If you do, it gains haste, and it's returned from the battlefield to its owner's hand at the beginning of the next end step.)
blocked_sentences: When this creature enters, create two 2/2 red Human Knight creature tokens with trample and haste.

needs.what: A 2/2 red Human Knight creature token with trample and haste registered in the token pool -- suggested id `human_knight_2_2_r_trample_haste`, matching the existing naming convention (`knight_2_2_w_vigilance`, `vampire_rogue_1_1_b_lifelink`): types ["Creature"], subtypes ["Human", "Knight"], power 2, toughness 2, colors ["R"], color_identity ["R"], keywords ["trample", "haste"], is_token true. This is the *same* token `forth_eorlingas` already asked for, so one definition unblocks both cards and no new engine behaviour is needed beyond adding it to `data/cards/tokens.cards.json` -- a card worker cannot add it, because `data/cards/` is outside the one file a worker may write. The general form of the request (either the token pool grows ahead of the cards that reference it, or `create_token` learns an inline token definition) is recorded on `forth_eorlingas` and is not restated as a separate need here.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `create_token` names a token only by card id: `loader.py:1794-1795` rejects the op without a `token` key, and `validate_token_references` at `loader.py:2160-2171` raises `create_token references unknown card` for any id that is not an already-loaded token card, so there is no inline `power`/`toughness`/`colors`/`subtypes`/`keywords` form to fall back on. All 29 tokens currently defined across `data/cards/` contain no red Human and no Knight other than `knight_2_2_w_vigilance` (white, vigilance, not a Human), and nothing at all with trample or haste; the nearest reds are `warrior_1_1_r` and `goblin_1_1_r` (1/1, wrong subtypes, no keywords) and the nearest Human is `human_1_1_w` (1/1, white, no Knight). Substituting any of them would change the tokens' size, colour, subtypes and both keywords -- on a five-mana creature whose entire non-dash text is those two bodies, that is most of the card -- and the `tokens` expectation key cannot be asserted for a token that does not exist, so the substitution would also be unverifiable.

closest_existing: token_pool (already requested by forth_eorlingas for this exact token, and by horn_of_gondor and oath_of_eorl for others)
rest_is_expressible: Dash is NOT blocked and needs nothing new -- it is the existing `evoke` alternative cost under a different label, exactly as `schema.py:390-396` documents ("dash and blitz are the same mechanism under different words"), and `flamerush_rider`'s gap record likewise leaves its dash line unblocked. The card would carry `"evoke": "{4}{R}{W}"`, `"evoke_label": "dash"`, and one triggered ability whose `text` is the printed dash line, with `trigger: {"event": "self_enters", "condition": {"evoked": true}}` -- the pattern `mulldrifter` uses in `data/cards/auto/templates.cards.json` -- and effects `grant_keyword` haste with `duration: "permanent"` on `{"self_only": true}` for "it gains haste", then `{"op": "delay", "step": "end_step", "effects": [{"op": "return_to_hand", "objects": {"self_only": true}}]}` for the bounce, which works because `DelayedTrigger` (`engine/structs.py:184-202`) keeps `source_oid` and `end_step` is in `turn.DELAY_STEPS`. The loader's half-a-cost guard is satisfied too: the `evoked` condition is read, so the cost is not orphaned. No partial answer was written, because the only other printed line is the blocked one -- a card carrying dash and nothing else would be a 4/4 that enters and makes no Knights, and the residual gate would reject it for leaving that line unclaimed. Once the token exists the whole card is a two-line answer, and the sandbox can assert it properly: `zone: "battlefield"`, `battlefield_count: 35` (32 + the creature + two Knights), and `tokens: {"id": "human_knight_2_2_r_trample_haste", "count": 2}` -- dash itself stays unasserted there, since the harness casts for the printed cost.
